text:
anna: quick follow-up on the observability RFC — I've sketched two pipeline options for logs/metrics/traces and wanted quick takes before I write the doc.

mike: thanks. can you summarize the tradeoffs? short bullets pls

anna: option A: central ingestion -> enrich -> route to long-term store. Pros: single enrichment step, easier cost attribution. Cons: amplification on spikes, harder to backpressure upstream.

linh: option B? 

anna: option B: edge enrichment and sampling near producers, then push to separate pipelines per signal. Pros: limits amplification, cheaper long-term. Cons: many enrichment implementations to maintain, risk of inconsistent tags across services.

rahul: my +1 to B if we solve tag consistency. We already have the config service; could push a small lib to standardize tags and versions.

mike: main question: where do we put cost attribution tags? in metrics only, or traces+logs too?

anna: thinking: put cost_account_id and workload_id on traces and metrics as canonical source, propagate to logs via trace_id. That way traces/metrics are queryable for cost and logs are joinable.

linh: agree. Also prefer immutable span names and add a 'span.service_version' tag to avoid brittle queries when names change.

observability-bot: deployment plan: canary the new enrichment lib to 5 services via feature flag. Link: https://deploys.redwood.internal/canary/341

mike: sampling strategy? don't want to lose low-volume expensive tails used for cost analysis.

anna: propose hierarchical sampling: keep 100% of traces that contain cost_account_id or workload_id above threshold; otherwise instrument-level reservoir sampling.

rahul: can we implement dynamic sampling rates pushed from the control plane? so we can bump sampling for a tenant during an incident.

linh: yes—we can push sample-rate config keyed by workload_id. small lib change.

mike: storage layout: store metrics + aggregated cost tags in ClickHouse, traces in Tempo-like system, logs in ES/LogStore. We need a cheap pre-join table for cost attribution queries.

anna: agreed. we should emit a daily cost-agg job that materializes (workload_id, day, tokens_generated, compute_ms, storage_bytes)

rahul: operational note: central enrichment (A) would require autoscaling headroom on the ingestion tier; B moves autoscaling to lots of app nodes. Both have different SRE profiles.

mike: ok looks like consensus for Option B with centralized config + immutable tag lib + hierarchical sampling + daily materialized cost table. Can we file a short RFC addendum and list the implementation milestones?

anna: will draft addendum this week. Milestones: 1) lib + config service changes, 2) canary 5 services, 3) pipeline routing + sampling config, 4) materialized cost job, 5) rollout and dashboards.

linh: ping me on the lib PR for API shape. I can take the tag-schema section.

observability-bot: :white_check_mark: Issue created: ORD-1245 - obsv-pipeline-addendum

deploy-bot: deploy of enironment-config v3 succeeded for canary group

mike: thanks everyone. Anna — post the addendum here and we'll do a short sync on Friday

anna: will do. :thumbsup:
